Governing law is the counterparty's (Kingdom of Saudi Arabia). AtliQ has no presence there. review.summary: Gulf Crown Hotels & Resorts Co. (Riyadh, KSA) sent its own MSA to AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd. The deal is USD 140,000 over 36 months to build a revenue management and guest analytics platform for nine hotels in Saudi Arabia. The most serious problem is the Al Noor non-compete (R-015), which is live: Al Noor's term runs to 14 March 2028, plus 18 months after that. It bars AtliQ and its Affiliates from providing data analytics, AI or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business in the GCC, and Saudi Arabia is in the GCC. The only waiver on record (R-046) covers the Seaside SOW alone. Signing would also make the warranty in Clause 9.1(d) untrue on day one. Possible further conflicts are the CloudSpan exclusivity (R-030), depending on which cloud platform is used, and the Crestline pricing promise (R-004). Other points: guest personal data under KSA PDPL with hosting in KSA; uncapped liability for confidentiality and data-protection breaches; liquidated damages at 1% of the whole Contract Value per week, capped at 10%; payment at 60 days; Saudi law and Riyadh courts; the Arabic text prevails but has not been provided; and termination pays only for accepted work.

The services are revenue management, guest analytics and AI/propensity models, which is exactly the restricted scope. The restriction binds AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd, the entity named here. It lasts for the Al Noor term (to 14 March 2028 unless terminated early) plus 18 months, so it is live today. Only a written waiver from Al Noor under its clause 12.4 would remove the conflict.

clauses.reason: The milestones finish at week 40, so the remaining term is presumably support. Note that the term would overlap the Al Noor restriction for its whole length.

clauses.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice if the other Party commits a material breach and fails to remedy such breach within thirty (30) days
clauses.reason: Mutual, with a cure period.

clauses.quote: the Company shall pay for all Services performed and accepted up to the date of termination.
clauses.reason: The checklist says "termination → they pay for work done". Work in progress on an unaccepted milestone would be unpaid, yet 6.5 requires AtliQ to hand it over. The right is also one-sided: AtliQ has no convenience exit.
clauses.past_positions: CloudSpan, Aug 2025: AtliQ asked for and got "mutual 90-day termination for convenience".

clauses.plain_english: Either party may terminate immediately on the other's insolvency.
clauses.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately if the other Party becomes insolvent

clauses.quote: the Service Provider shall deliver to the Company all Deliverables and work in progress, and shall provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to sixty (60) days.

clauses.quote: All Deliverables specifically created for the Company under this Agreement shall, upon payment in full, become the property of the Company.
clauses.reason: This matches the checklist ("client owns what we build for them, we keep our own stuff") and AtliQ's usual position (R-003, R-012, R-020). Check that no freelancer-owned components are used: R-023 shows Rohan Iyer kept ownership of his Work Product.

clauses.plain_english: Reasonable skill and care, 90-day conformity warranty, and authority to contract.
clauses.quote: the Deliverables shall conform in all material respects to the specifications in Schedule 1 for a period of ninety (90) days following acceptance
clauses.reason: Standard and time-limited.

clauses.plain_english: AtliQ warrants that no other agreement stops or restricts it from doing this work.
clauses.quote: it is not bound by any agreement or restriction which would prevent or restrict it from performing the Services for the Company.
clauses.reason: This would be untrue because of the live Al Noor non-compete (R-015, R-047). It may also be untrue because of the CloudSpan exclusivity (R-030), depending on the platform. Do not sign until the restrictions are resolved.

clauses.plain_english: AtliQ fixes defects notified during the warranty period at its own cost.
clauses.quote: The Service Provider shall, at its own cost, remedy any defect notified by the Company during the warranty period.
clauses.reason: Standard.

clauses.plain_english: Neither side is liable for indirect or consequential loss or loss of profits.
clauses.quote: Neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, special or consequential loss, or loss of profits
clauses.reason: Mutual.

clauses.plain_english: Each side's liability is capped at the Contract Value, except fraud, wilful misconduct and breaches of confidentiality or data protection, which are uncapped.
clauses.quote: Save in respect of liability arising from fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality) or Clause 13 (Data Protection), each Party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the Contract Value.
clauses.reason: A 1x cap matches the checklist. However, liability for confidentiality and data-protection breaches is unlimited, on a deal handling hotel guest and loyalty personal data. That is the likeliest serious claim, so the exposure is effectively unlimited. Checklist: "liability → 1x fees. NOT unlimited." Consider a separate, higher cap (a multiple of fees) for data breaches.
clauses.past_positions: Kessler Mobility, Jan 2026: K said "Unlimited liability on a €120k deal means one bad incident … and the company is gone" and offered 1x fees with carve-outs; the deal was lost. PayTrack, Jan 2025: "Liability cap stays 1x fees."

clauses.reason: Broadly reciprocal, and AtliQ does not cover the client's own negligence. The indemnity is not carved out of the 10.2 cap, so it appears capped. Because 11.1 covers "the Deliverables" without excluding Company-supplied materials, a human should confirm this reading.
clauses.past_positions: PayTrack, Jan 2025: AtliQ rejected an indemnity covering the client's negligence and agreed a mutual indemnity instead.

clauses.quote: Time shall be of the essence in respect of the Milestone dates set out in Schedule 3.
clauses.reason: This may let the client treat any milestone slip as a serious breach giving a right to terminate, on top of the LDs. Its effect under Saudi law needs counsel.

clauses.quote: an amount equal to one percent (1%) of the Contract Value for each week or part thereof of delay.
clauses.reason: The LDs are capped ("shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the Contract Value"), so this is not open-ended. But they are calculated on total fees rather than the delayed milestone. There is also no exclusion for delays caused by the Company; only Force Majeure is excluded (12.5). This draft mirrors the Al Noor exception.
clauses.past_positions: Acme (Mar 2025), Northwind (Jun 2025) and Trustline (Aug 2026): each settled at "0.5% of milestone fee per week, cap 5% of milestone, client delays excluded". Al Noor, Mar 2025: K said "Approving 10% of total fees as a strategic exception for Al Noor only — not our new standard", and the weekly 1% was still calculated on the milestone.

clauses.plain_english: The Company may deduct LDs from any payment due.
clauses.quote: The Company may deduct any liquidated damages due from any amount payable to the Service Provider under this Agreement.
clauses.reason: Unilateral set-off, with no requirement that the LDs be agreed or undisputed first.

clauses.plain_english: No LDs for delay caused by Force Majeure.

It does not mention Gulf Crown, but Al Noor confidential information must not be used here.

clauses.plain_english: AtliQ must apply appropriate security measures and notify breaches within 72 hours.
clauses.quote: shall notify the Company of any personal data breach within seventy-two (72) hours of becoming aware of it.
clauses.reason: 72 hours is longer than other AtliQ commitments (24h, 48h, 6h), so it is operationally achievable.

clauses.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws and regulations in force in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
clauses.reason: The rules engine flags this: it is the counterparty's law and AtliQ has no presence in KSA. It is acceptable only as a deliberate trade, given the cost of enforcing or defending abroad. Checklist: "gov law → ours (India for Pvt Ltd)".

review.summary: Lakeshore Grocers Inc. (Illinois, USA) MSA on Lakeshore's paper, naming AtliQ Inc, for data engineering and BI work: lakehouse migration, pipelines, semantic layer and Power BI. SOW-1 is USD 64,000. Delay damages, payment terms, IP and non-solicit are close to positions AtliQ has taken before. The main finding is a register conflict: the Exhibit A rates ($72 / $55 / $50 per hour, fixed for 24 months) are below the rates in the Crestline Retail MSA ($85 / $62 / $58). Crestline's live pricing promise (R-004, until 31 July 2027) applies to 'substantially similar services' by AtliQ Inc or its affiliates. There is also a possible IP conflict if AtliQ's PipeKit accelerator, already assigned to Northwind (R-026), is reused here as a 'Vendor Tool'. Other points for review: uncapped liability for confidentiality, indemnity and gross negligence claims (9.2); SIAC arbitration in Singapore for a US entity under Illinois law (13.3); Exhibit C security schedule not attached; and the rules engine's financial-data flag.

review.summary: TravelHub FZ-LLC (Dubai Internet City) client draft for a USD 52,000 fixed-fee build of AI features for a consumer travel app. The features include a Partner Hotel Ranking Module covering UAE and KSA hotels, and the counterparty earns commission on hotel bookings. This appears to fall squarely within the live Al Noor GCC hospitality non-compete (R-015, reaffirmed by R-047), which covers hotel distribution providers and binds AtliQ's affiliates, including AtliQ Inc. The Feb 2026 Al Noor consent (R-046) covers Seaside Hotels only. The entity set-up is inconsistent: AtliQ Inc (US) is the contracting party, but clause 7.1 has AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd invoice under its GSTIN, and the rules engine flags this as an entity conflict. Other points for the reviewer: governing law and courts are onshore Dubai; the liability cap is based on fees paid in the prior 12 months, with uncapped carve-outs; and UAE/KSA guest personal data is in scope. The rest of the commercial terms (30-day payment, IP split, mutual confidentiality, pay-for-work-done on termination, no LDs) match AtliQ's checklist positions. Suggested next step: escalate.

review.summary: FinServe Capital's own form, labelled a Mutual NDA, sent ahead of the 1 October data walkthrough. Despite the title, nearly every obligation binds only AtliQ (the "Recipient"). Only FinServe's information is protected, and only FinServe may use Residuals. The draft also adds terms that go beyond a normal NDA: a 12-month post-termination non-compete covering every bank, NBFC, wealth manager, broker and fintech in India (Clause 8.1); a one-way 24-month no-hire covering FinServe and its Affiliates (Clause 8.2); an uncapped one-way indemnity (Clause 10.2); and survival 'in perpetuity' (Clause 7.2), which may also extend the covenants. Clause 8.1 appears to collide with AtliQ's live Trustline NBFC engagement (collections analytics for an Indian NBFC lender) and possibly with PayTrack. Data in scope includes customer and portfolio data from an RBI/SEBI-regulated lender, which the rules engine flags as regulated financial data. The entity (AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd) and governing law (India, Mumbai courts) match the expected position per the rules engine. Suggested next step: escalate. This is a brief for a human reviewer, not legal advice.

register_conflicts.incoming_clause_quote: the Recipient shall not, during the term of this Agreement and for a period of twelve (12) months after its termination, provide services similar to those contemplated by the Proposed Transaction to any Competitor.
register_conflicts.register_clause_quote: Upon full payment, intellectual property in the Deliverables developed specifically for the Company shall vest in the Company. The Service Provider retains its pre-existing intellectual property and grants the Company a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use it as incorporated in the Deliverables.
register_conflicts.explanation: Clause 1.5 defines Competitor as "any bank, non-banking financial company, wealth manager, broker or fintech platform operating in India that offers products substantially similar to those of the Company". The Proposed Transaction is "data analytics and reporting solutions for the Company's lending and wealth businesses". AtliQ is currently delivering collections analytics (data mart, early-warning scorecard, Power BI dashboards) to Trustline NBFC Limited, an Indian NBFC lender. The register shows that MSA running for one year from 15 August 2026 (R-053 to R-056). The restriction applies 'during the term', i.e. from signature. Signing would therefore likely put the ongoing Trustline work, and any extension or new SOW, in breach from day one, and bar it for 12 months after termination. Whether Trustline's products are 'substantially similar' to FinServe's lending products is a human judgement, but on the face of the register they overlap.

register_conflicts.incoming_clause_quote: the Recipient shall not, during the term of this Agreement and for a period of twelve (12) months after its termination, provide services similar to those contemplated by the Proposed Transaction to any Competitor.

register_conflicts.explanation: PayTrack is an Indian fintech (payments reconciliation and merchant settlement) with a live MSA, two years from 22 January 2025 (R-009 to R-011). The definition of Competitor includes any "fintech platform operating in India that offers products substantially similar to those of the Company". FinServe's named businesses are lending and wealth, so overlap with PayTrack's payments product is uncertain. If it overlaps, continuing or renewing PayTrack analytics work would be restricted. A human needs to check FinServe's and its Affiliates' product lines.

review.no_conflicts_statement: Conflicts found: 1 conflict and 1 possible conflict against the 49 commitments on the register (see register_conflicts). No other register entries were found to conflict. Orbit entries R-001/R-002 have expired and are not relevant.

clauses.quote: (together with its Affiliates, the "Company"); and
clauses.reason: The AtliQ entity is correct for an Indian counterparty (rules engine OK). However, defining AtliQ solely as 'Recipient' and FinServe as discloser is why the 'mutual' NDA is one-way in practice. Folding all FinServe Affiliates into 'Company' also widens who counts as a Competitor (8.1) and whose staff are covered by the no-hire (8.2). The Effective Date blank must be filled.

clauses.quote: the Parties anticipate a mutual exchange of information
clauses.reason: Acceptable as written. Note the recital promises a mutual exchange that the operative clauses do not deliver. This is useful leverage when asking for the clauses to be made mutual.

clauses.plain_english: Standard control-based definition of Affiliate.
clauses.quote: "Affiliate" means any entity that controls, is controlled by or is under common control with a Party.

clauses.plain_english: Only information disclosed by FinServe to AtliQ is protected. AtliQ's own information (architecture, methods, pricing) gets no protection.
clauses.quote: disclosed or made available by or on behalf of the Company to the Recipient or its Representatives
clauses.reason: This is the core one-sidedness. AtliQ is expected to share its technology approach during scoping, and that material would be unprotected. Ask for the definition to cover information disclosed by either Party.
clauses.past_positions: GlobalMart NDA, Mar 2026: one-way NDA rejected; K: "We only sign mutual — we'll be sharing our architecture too." They agreed to mutual. Checklist (Karandeep, 2024): "NDAs → just sign if mutual".

clauses.plain_english: Representatives are directors, officers, employees and professional advisers. Contractors, freelancers and affiliates are not included.
clauses.quote: "Representatives" means a Party's directors, officers, employees and professional advisers.
clauses.reason: AtliQ could not share FinServe information with freelancers or subcontractors. That may be fine at evaluation stage, but would restrict any delivery that relies on contractors. The reviewer should decide whether contractors bound in writing need to be added.
clauses.past_positions: Meridian Healthcare NDA, Jul 2026: signed within the hour with no changes. The register (R-050) now records that Meridian information can go only to employees, excluding freelancers and subcontractors.

clauses.quote: "Competitor" means any bank, non-banking financial company, wealth manager, broker or fintech platform operating in India that offers products substantially similar to those of the Company.
clauses.reason: This very broad definition drives the non-compete in 8.1. It appears to capture Trustline NBFC (live client) and possibly PayTrack.
clauses.past_positions: Al Noor MSA, Mar 2025: K narrowed a worldwide non-compete: "Worldwide for three years would stop us working in hospitality altogether."

clauses.plain_english: AtliQ must use FinServe information only for the deal, share it only with Representatives on a need-to-know basis, follow FinServe's security policy as notified from time to time, and is responsible for its Representatives.
clauses.quote: apply security measures no less stringent than those required under the Company's information-security policy as notified to the Recipient from time to time
clauses.reason: The obligations bind only the Recipient. The security policy has not been provided and can change unilaterally. Ask for a copy before the walkthrough, and for the obligations to apply to both Parties.
clauses.past_positions: Crestline (R-005) and Brightwater (R-045) also tie AtliQ to client security requirements 'as updated'. Brightwater was signed without redlines ("Looks standard, signing now"), and the negotiation history points to an April post-mortem on that deal.

clauses.quote: The Recipient shall not, without the Company's prior written consent, disclose to any person the fact that discussions are taking place or any of their terms.
clauses.reason: Commercially low-risk, but one-way. FinServe is free to disclose. Ask for it to be mutual.

clauses.quote: The obligations in Clause 2 shall not apply to information which the Recipient can demonstrate by contemporaneous written evidence:
clauses.reason: The independent-development exception is missing. That matters because AtliQ already builds lending analytics for other clients, e.g. Trustline's early-warning scorecard. Without it, similar work done independently could be argued to derive from FinServe's information. The evidence standard is also strict.

clauses.plain_english: If law or a regulator requires disclosure, AtliQ must give FinServe prior written notice and disclose only the minimum.
clauses.quote: it shall give the Company prior written notice and disclose only such part as it is legally required to disclose.
clauses.reason: Prior notice is unconditional. Some regulatory demands prohibit notice. Ask to add 'to the extent legally permitted'.

clauses.plain_english: FinServe alone may use anything its people remember, including AtliQ's ideas and techniques, for any purpose, including procuring products and services.
clauses.quote: the Company shall be free to use Residuals for any purpose, including the development, marketing and procurement of products and services
clauses.reason: This is one-sided. Combined with 1.2, it means AtliQ's architecture and approach shared during scoping could be reused by FinServe or handed to another vendor. Ask for deletion or a mutual, narrow version.
clauses.past_positions: GlobalMart NDA, Mar 2026 (K): "we'll be sharing our architecture too." Checklist: "IP → client owns what we build for them, we keep our own stuff".

clauses.plain_english: On request, AtliQ must return or destroy everything within 5 business days and give a director-signed certificate.
clauses.quote: return or permanently destroy all Confidential Information and certify such destruction in writing signed by a director.
clauses.reason: The timeline is tight and there is no carve-out for automatic backups or legally required retention. It is also one-way. This is a judgement call.

clauses.plain_english: AtliQ must co-operate with, and give records access to, FinServe and its regulators (RBI, SEBI) in relation to the information.
clauses.quote: agrees to provide such co-operation and access to records as the Company or its regulators may reasonably require in connection with the Confidential Information.
clauses.reason: The rules engine flags financial customer data in India, which means checking RBI outsourcing rules and the DPDP Act. Confirm with counsel what will actually be shared at the 1 Oct walkthrough. The audit obligation itself is in line with commitments already given to regulated clients.
clauses.past_positions: The register shows similar regulator-audit terms already accepted: Trustline R-056 (RBI may inspect and audit) and PayTrack R-011 (PayTrack and regulators may audit).

clauses.plain_english: AtliQ must comply with the DPDP Act for personal data and report any personal data breach within six hours.
clauses.quote: shall notify the Company of any personal data breach within six (6) hours.

clauses.past_positions: Register: Trustline R-055 already commits AtliQ to a six-hour incident report 'of becoming aware'. PayTrack R-011 is 24 hours; Meridian R-051 is 24 hours.

clauses.quote: shall continue until terminated by either Party on thirty (30) days' written notice.

clauses.past_positions: CloudSpan, Aug 2025: K obtained mutual 90-day termination for convenience.

'All obligations' could also be read to override the 12- and 24-month limits in Clause 8. Ask for a fixed survival period, e.g. a number of years, and to exclude Clause 8 from it.
clauses.past_positions: Meridian NDA, Jul 2026 (signed unchanged): obligations survive 3 years after expiry (R-050/R-051).

clauses.plain_english: During the term and for 12 months after it, AtliQ may not provide analytics/reporting services similar to this deal to any Indian bank, NBFC, wealth manager, broker or fintech with similar products.
clauses.quote: the Recipient shall not, during the term of this Agreement and for a period of twelve (12) months after its termination, provide services similar to those contemplated by the Proposed Transaction to any Competitor.
clauses.reason: It appears to conflict with the live Trustline NBFC engagement (R-053 to R-056) and possibly PayTrack (R-008 to R-011). It applies from signature, with no deal yet won, and would block AtliQ from Indian BFSI analytics generally. A non-compete is unusual in an NDA. Ask for deletion.

Bhavin at the time: "we'll never do another hotel in the Gulf anyway". A consent letter for Seaside was nonetheless needed by Feb 2026.

review.summary: LoopMart Retail Private Limited (India, retail) has sent its standard two-way NDA ahead of a possible customer analytics and demand-forecasting engagement. The NDA is with AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd. Obligations are worded for whichever party receives information, so they bind both sides equally. Governing law is India, with Bengaluru courts. The rules engine found the entity, governing law and paperwork as expected. The NDA has no non-compete, non-solicit, exclusivity, pricing or IP transfer. Clause 8.2 expressly leaves both parties free to work with third parties. It also allows disclosure to subcontractors, so it does not repeat the restrictions AtliQ accepted in the Meridian NDA. One item is for a human to judge: Clause 5 contemplates sharing personal data (the Purpose covers 'sales and customer data'). It requires DPDP Act compliance but sets no breach-notice timeframe. You may want to clarify what customer data LoopMart will share at this stage. Two placeholders need filling: the Effective Date and AtliQ's signature block. No register conflicts were found. Note for any later engagement (not this NDA): retail analytics pricing will be subject to the Crestline MFN (R-004), and any platform choice may touch the CloudSpan exclusivity (R-030).
